# VenueMind complete agent reference

This file is generated from the same public structured documentation source as the VenueMind docs site.

# Venue planning, built for agents and humans

A versioned spatial-planning system where agents inspect, propose, validate, and compare—while humans retain the commit decision.

## The operating model

1. Inspect the accepted Plan and stable object IDs.
2. Preview non-destructive Changes on a Proposal branch.
3. Validate deterministic Constraints.
4. Review the ghost diff in VenueMind.
5. Approve into the next immutable Plan Version.

## One planner, three surfaces

- VenueMind Studio — visible planning, comparison, approval, undo, and export.
- Native WebMCP — tools registered directly by the open planning page.
- VenueMind MCP server — the same tools over stdio for external agent hosts.

## Start here

- [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart)
- [Core concepts](/docs/concepts)
- [Tool reference](/docs/webmcp)

---

# Quickstart

Open the Studio, inspect the seeded SummitForward Plan, and run the complete supervised Proposal loop.

## Run the Studio

```bash
npm install
npm run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0 --port 4173
```

Open the printed local URL. The WebMCP status changes to Native when the browser discovers the registered tools.

## Run the MCP server

```bash
npm run build:mcp
node packages/mcp-server/dist/index.js
```

The server uses stdio. Standard output is reserved for MCP protocol messages; operational logs go to standard error.

## First planning loop

1. Call venue.get_project_brief and venue.inspect_layout.
2. Call venue.preview_revision with a measurable goal.
3. Call venue.validate_layout.
4. Review the Proposal in VenueMind.
5. Approve in the Studio and export the new Plan Version.

---

# Core concepts

VenueMind separates accepted spatial truth from agent-authored possibilities.

## Project Lifecycle

Project duplication starts a new version-1 lineage with new Project, Plan, Event Brief, Requirement, Proposal, and Change IDs plus source-Plan provenance. Rename, pin, recent-open, archive, restore, and typed-confirmation soft delete preserve the complete snapshot. Deleted Projects remain recoverable for seven days.

## Venue, Room, and Inventory Templates

Venue and Room Templates are reusable, versioned physical definitions. Every Project pins exact template versions while its placed objects keep separate Project-scoped IDs. Inventory Item Templates cover furniture, seating, barriers, staging, AV, catering, signage, and queues with dimensions, weight, power, capacity, cost, and availability metadata.

## Template Updates and Project Overrides

A newer Room Template produces a reviewable Proposal containing only safe differences. Field-level Project Overrides remain authoritative, unavailable additions and deletions are reported for review, and the accepted Plan remains unchanged until normal Validation and human Approval succeed.

## Plan and Plan Version

A Plan is the accepted spatial arrangement for one event in one venue room. Every accepted revision is immutable and identified by a Plan Version.

## Event Brief and Requirement

The Event Brief stores event identity, attendance, occupancy mode, and stable prioritized Requirements. Coverage maps measurable Requirements to Constraint evidence for both the accepted Plan and the active Proposal.

## Room Boundary and Footprint

Every Plan uses one real-world spatial frame measured in metres. The Room Boundary defines valid space; each object has a typed Footprint, elevation, layer, and stable ID. Distance is normalized to millimetre precision and rotation to a tenth of a degree.

## Operational geometry

Doors and exits are line Footprints with clear-width and access metadata. Corridors, aisles, and service lanes are typed Route Graph edges. Restricted Zones are polygonal or rectangular Footprints with explicit access and placement rules.

## Accessible infrastructure

Accessible Seat Samples bind designated representative seats to focal-point rays. Door Clearance Zones are derived from Door geometry and maneuvering metadata. Temporary Ramps carry rise, run, clear width, landing, edge-protection, and handrail evidence.

## Capacity and Occupancy Zones

Capacity evidence reconciles Seating Section counts into stable Occupancy Zones and the full Plan. Each scope has independent minimum and maximum bounds. Every Proposal Change records isolated section, zone, placed, effective, and operational-load deltas against the accepted Plan.

## Circulation and Egress Evidence

The walkable Route Graph excludes edges obstructed by placement geometry. Validation derives Exit Approach Zones, shortest egress paths, Critical Route Edges, component-level Bottleneck Loads, phase profiles, and isolated congestion deltas for every Proposal Change.

## Proposal, Branch, and Change

A Proposal is a non-destructive candidate based on exactly one Plan Version. Branches preserve competing strategies; Changes are stable, inspectable spatial differences inside a Proposal.

## Proposal-safe editing

Studio transforms, placement, grouping, zoning, clipboard operations, and layout presets all create Proposal Changes through the same command interface used by agents. The accepted Plan is never edited in place. Each command has a stable Change ID, supports undo and redo, appears in the Activity Ledger, and remains subject to Validation and human Approval.

- Selection, box selection, pan, zoom, grid snapping, alignment, distribution, and numeric transforms share canonical metre-based geometry.
- Layer visibility and layer locks are local workspace controls; object Locks are durable Project records enforced by the planner.
- Measurements are read-only and evaluate the active Proposal candidate without creating a Change.

## Proposal Conflicts

Conflict detection returns stale-base, deleted-dependency, Lock, same-object, geometry-overlap, and Constraint-regression records with stable IDs and permitted outcomes. Human keep-plan and keep-proposal choices preserve unchanged Change IDs. Manual Resolution replaces only transformed Changes with new stable IDs and explicit lineage, then reruns Validation and appends the outcome to the Activity Ledger.

## Proposal comparison and decisions

Branch comparison overlays the accepted Plan with both candidates and reports added, removed, moved, rotated, resized, and metadata differences. Capacity, access width, circulation load, egress distance, sightline coverage, deterministic risk, estimated inventory cost, and Constraint outcomes are evaluated from each candidate.

Branches keep human notes and Proposal revision history. Any revision can seed a new Branch; archive and restore preserve that history. A human decision checkpoint records the chosen Branch, rejected alternatives, comparison fingerprint, and rationale in the Activity Ledger before Approval.

## Comments and immutable anchors

Comments are collaboration records, not planning mutations. Each Comment binds permanently to a Project, Plan Version, Proposal, Change, Constraint, or metre-based coordinate. Branch switches and later Plan Versions never retarget that anchor.

Open, resolved, and reopened states retain author, timestamps, mentions, and complete edit history. Decision-relevant Comments are included in audit exports; coordinate Comments render as numbered annotation pins in the Studio.

## Operational exports

The shared export command produces layered SVG with stable object IDs and accessible labels, a two-page vector PDF with Plan and Validation evidence, a one-page print-safe Emergency Plan, RFC4180 object, inventory, staffing, production, catering, and replenishment schedules, staffing and production maps, structured JSON or text, and a portable audit package bound to geometry, ledger, and replay fingerprints.

- PDF output identifies the evaluated Proposal and accepted base Plan Version.
- The Emergency Plan PDF renders routes, exits, safety infrastructure, readiness, degraded-scenario outcomes, and its evidence fingerprint without raster dependencies.
- Inventory schedules reconcile requested stock, availability, cost, weight, and power.
- Operational exports derive from the same accepted Plan and deterministic evidence used by Approval.
- Audit packages include decision-relevant Comments, public command receipts, Emergency Reviews, assumptions, and scenario evidence.
- Studio and agent tools invoke the same read-only export command.

## Constraint and Validation

Constraints are measurable conditions. Validation deterministically evaluates locks, accessibility, capacity, sightlines, circulation, production, catering, emergency readiness, and congestion against actual and threshold values. Byte-equivalent results are reused only when the immutable Validation input fingerprint and its canonical input both match.

## Scenario and Simulation Run

A Scenario is an immutable set of assumptions, phases, time horizon, sample count, and deterministic seed evaluated against one exact Proposal Branch geometry fingerprint. A Simulation Run stores engine version, progress, partial checkpoints, confidence metadata, and its completed, cancelled, or failed outcome.

Simulation is probabilistic evidence and never becomes Constraint evidence. A changed Proposal cancels its obsolete active Run; identical immutable inputs reuse the cached normalized result. Compatible completed Runs require matching Scenario definition fingerprints and engine versions.

## Ingress and egress

The ingress-egress model combines monotonic arrival and departure curves with aggregate Mobility Profiles. Profiles contain only a stable cohort ID, population share, speed factor, and accessible-route requirement; no person-level records enter the engine.

- Infrastructure is derived from the exact Plan or Proposal Branch: entrances, exits, checkpoints, Doors, stairs, elevators, Corridors, Aisles, accessible routes, occupied Sections, and Route Graph paths.
- Every result includes zone and full-venue clearance, bottleneck duration and affected occupancy, accessible-route performance, normal versus emergency assumptions, and time-keyed Density Frames.
- Density cells bind aggregate persons-per-square-metre estimates to stable object IDs and can be replayed in the Studio.
- Branch comparisons expose total clearance, worst bottleneck, and accessible-route deltas without changing the Plan or Validation.

## Queue simulation

The queue model supports registration, security, cloakroom, food, beverage, restroom, merchandise, and transport operations. Seeded runs model arrivals, service per server, parallel servers, abandonment patience, priority lanes, and spatial buffer capacity.

- Results include average, median, and p95 wait, maximum queue length, abandonment, overflow risk, and lane evidence.
- Spill evidence names exact nearby Route and Exit object IDs when p95 queue area exceeds the modeled buffer.
- A measurable server and buffer option is emitted only with deterministic spatial preflight and requires explicit human action.
- Previewing an option creates an ordinary violet ghost Change and immediately runs deterministic Validation; the Simulation Result never changes or approves the Plan.

## Staffing and operations

A Staffing Plan versions role headcounts, skills, shifts, zone requirements, handoff policy, and maximum walking distance alongside the venue Plan. Staff Posts are typed spatial objects with stable IDs, coverage-zone links, and role assignments by shift.

- Coverage evidence evaluates entrances, exits, accessible routes, stages, and service areas by exact zone and post IDs.
- Walking-distance gaps, insufficient role headcount, and short shift handoffs remain explicit auditable results.
- Staff-only service routes are modeled separately from attendee circulation and never alter accessible-route Validation.
- The shared export command produces an RFC4180 staffing schedule and an SVG post map without mutating Plan truth.

## AV and production planning

Production Readiness Evidence is deterministic Constraint evidence for the exact visible Plan or Proposal. It binds screens, projectors, speakers, cameras, control desks, Cable Routes, Utility Points, Rigging Points, backstage zones, and inventory instances by stable ID.

- Projector throw ratios use exact projector-to-screen geometry and viewable width.
- Seat-to-screen rays, speaker coverage cones, camera ranges, and control sightlines retain their sampled object and obstruction IDs.
- Every accessible Cable Crossing requires an allowed overhead or cable-ramp treatment.
- Circuit and Rigging Loads reconcile rated infrastructure against placed equipment demand; inventory shortages remain blocking production evidence.
- The shared export command produces a production CSV and production-only SVG map without changing accepted Plan truth.

## Catering and service planning

Service Capacity Evidence evaluates the exact visible Plan or Proposal across arrival, break, and meal phases. Typed Service Stations link throughput, queue buffers, accessible counter height, support spaces, water, Replenishment Routes, and inventory by stable ID.

- Queue Zones fail when they spill into public circulation or emergency exits.
- Service and support objects retain measured separation from production and emergency infrastructure.
- Controlled Replenishment Route crossings remain visible circulation impacts; uncontrolled crossings block Approval.
- Dietary Options and Allergen Labels describe stations only. Attendee health records are rejected at the geometry boundary.
- Branch comparison includes service capacity, queue risk, circulation crossings, and accessible Service Points.
- The shared export command produces Service Station and Replenishment Route schedules without changing accepted Plan truth.

## Emergency planning

An Emergency Plan versions exits, assembly points, responder access lanes, fire-equipment coverage, first-aid posts, command posts, operating assumptions, and three required Degraded Scenarios alongside accepted Plan truth.

- Emergency readiness is a deterministic hard Constraint over exact geometry, capacities, infrastructure IDs, and power metadata.
- Blocked-exit and unavailable-corridor scenarios remove named graph inputs and retain affected zones, Alternative Emergency Routes, available exit capacity, shortfall, and unresolved hard failures.
- Power-loss scenarios remove named circuits and verify backup duration for emergency infrastructure.
- Any Proposal that changes emergency infrastructure requires a separate authorized Emergency Review bound to the Proposal, base version, Validation, evidence fingerprint, assumptions, reviewer identity, and role.
- The audit package retains every review and scenario fingerprint; the shared export command produces a one-page vector Emergency Plan.

## Warning Waiver

A warning never disappears from Validation evidence. Approval requires a human-authored Warning Waiver bound to its Constraint, Proposal base version, and Validation input fingerprint. Approval carries that disposition into the resulting Plan Version; changed Proposals require a new waiver.

## Object Lock

A Lock protects one object property class: position, rotation, dimension, deletion, or role. Venue-template Locks are inherited with the accepted geometry; human Project Locks are temporary, reason-coded records outside the immutable Plan and can be explicitly released. Conflicts expose the Lock ID, type, source, object, and Change.

## Route Graph and Spatial Evidence

Validation derives route paths, clear widths, usable area, section capacity, phase loads, focal-point rays, viewing angles, and obstruction IDs from canonical geometry. Every result carries geometry and evidence fingerprints.

## Approval and Activity Ledger

Approval is the explicit human decision that commits a validated Proposal. Every human and agent action is appended to an ordered Activity Ledger.

# Create your first Project

Create a durable empty Project, open its canonical Plan, and confirm its first Validation result.

## Prerequisites

```bash
npm install
npm run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0 --port 4173
```

- Keep the development process running.
- Open http://localhost:4173/projects.

## Create and open

1. Select NEW PROJECT.
2. Open the new Project card.
3. Confirm the Studio header shows Plan v1.0.
4. Open the Event Brief and set the event identity, attendance target, occupancy mode, and measurable requirements.
5. Save the brief; unresolved measurable requirements remain visible until they map to Constraints.

## Completion criteria

- The Project appears in the Project index after navigation and reload.
- The Plan uses metres, stable Project-scoped IDs, and an empty accepted object set.
- Validation returns pass for the valid empty starting geometry.
- The Project record reports remote persistence or an explicit local recovery state.

## Next workflow

- [Run the supervised planning loop](/docs/tutorial-supervised-loop)

## Verify the workflow

Run the executable fixture from the repository root. Completion requires a zero exit code.

```bash
node --test tests/empty-project.test.mjs tests/project-store.test.mjs
```

# Run the supervised planning loop

Inspect, preview, validate, review, approve, and export one versioned venue revision.

## Prepare

1. Open /studio/project-summit-forward in a WebMCP-capable host.
2. Confirm the WebMCP diagnostic status is READY.
3. Keep the accepted Plan visible while the agent works.

## Inspect accepted truth

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.get_project_brief",
  "input": {}
}
```

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.inspect_layout",
  "input": {}
}
```

Retain the returned Plan Version, Proposal ID, stable object IDs, Locks, and correlation metadata.

## Preview a measurable outcome

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.preview_revision",
  "input": {
    "goal": "Reduce entrance congestion while preserving accessible routes",
    "idempotencyKey": "tutorial-preview-001",
    "correlationId": "tutorial-loop-001"
  }
}
```

The violet ghosts are Proposal Changes. The accepted Plan remains unchanged.

## Validate exact evidence

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.validate_layout",
  "input": {}
}
```

- Resolve every hard failure before review.
- A human must disposition every waivable warning.
- The Validation fingerprint must match the visible Proposal candidate.

## Review, approve, and export

1. Compare each violet Change with the accepted Plan.
2. Select Approve proposal in the Studio only when Validation passes and required reviews are complete.
3. Confirm the immutable Plan Version advances and the Approval appears in the Activity Ledger.
4. Export VM JSON or PDF from the Studio, or call venue.export_plan after Approval.

## Completion criteria

- The agent never invokes Approval.
- Exactly one human Approval creates exactly one Plan Version.
- The export identifies the new version and carries Validation and ledger evidence.

## Verify the workflow

Run the executable fixture from the repository root. Completion requires a zero exit code.

```bash
node --test tests/webmcp-conformance.test.mjs tests/venue-planner.test.mjs
```

# Compare access-first and capacity-first branches

Create two competing Proposal Branches, validate both, and record a human decision from measurable evidence.

## Create both strategies

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.create_proposal_branch",
  "input": {
    "name": "Access first",
    "strategy": "access-first",
    "goal": "Maximize accessible route clearance",
    "idempotencyKey": "tutorial-access-branch-001"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.create_proposal_branch",
  "input": {
    "name": "Capacity first",
    "strategy": "balanced",
    "goal": "Increase usable seating without reducing required clearances",
    "idempotencyKey": "tutorial-capacity-branch-001"
  }
}
```

## Develop and validate independently

1. Switch to Access first, preview its goal, and call venue.validate_layout.
2. Switch to Capacity first, preview its goal, and call venue.validate_layout.
3. Keep both Branch IDs and Validation fingerprints.
4. Do not reuse one Branch result as evidence for the other.

## Compare evidence

Use the Branch IDs returned by the two create calls. In a fresh seeded Project they are branch-2 and branch-3.

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.compare_proposal_branches",
  "input": {
    "leftBranchId": "branch-2",
    "rightBranchId": "branch-3"
  }
}
```

- Review capacity, access width, circulation, egress, sightlines, risk, inventory cost, and Constraint deltas.
- Open Plan history → Branches → Compare to inspect the spatial overlay.
- Enter a decision note and choose the evidence-backed Branch.

## Completion criteria

- Both Branches retain independent Changes and Validation results.
- The chosen and rejected Branch IDs, comparison fingerprint, and rationale appear in the Activity Ledger.
- The accepted Plan remains unchanged until a separate human Approval.

## Verify the workflow

Run the executable fixture from the repository root. Completion requires a zero exit code.

```bash
node --test tests/venue-planner.test.mjs
```

---

# Resolve a stale Proposal

Rebase a Proposal onto newer accepted truth without losing stable Change lineage or bypassing conflicts.

## Create the stale state

1. Create two Proposal Branches from the same accepted Plan Version.
2. Validate and approve the first Branch in the Studio.
3. Switch to the second Branch; its base version now trails the accepted Plan.
4. Confirm the Branch shows STALE before attempting further review.

## Detect conflicts

Use the Branch ID returned when you created the second Branch.

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.detect_proposal_conflicts",
  "input": {
    "branchId": "branch-3"
  }
}
```

- Read every conflict type, affected object ID, blocking state, and permitted resolution.
- A deleted dependency or effective Lock must remain explicit.

## Rebase and resolve

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.rebase_proposal",
  "input": {
    "branchId": "branch-3",
    "idempotencyKey": "tutorial-rebase-001"
  }
}
```

1. Resolve remaining same-object or geometry conflicts with keep-plan, keep-proposal, or manual resolution only where the conflict permits it.
2. Run venue.validate_layout again.
3. Review any transformed Change with its new ID and lineage.

## Completion criteria

- Unchanged Changes retain their stable Change IDs.
- Transformed Changes receive new IDs with explicit lineage.
- Validation evaluates the rebased fingerprint.
- Approval is enabled only after all blocking conflicts and hard failures are cleared.

## Verify the workflow

Run the executable fixture from the repository root. Completion requires a zero exit code.

```bash
node --test tests/venue-planner.test.mjs
```

---

# Audit an approved Plan Version

Verify approval authority, deterministic evidence, ledger integrity, and replay for one immutable Plan Version.

## Collect the evidence

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.inspect_layout",
  "input": {}
}
```

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.get_validation_evidence",
  "input": {
    "constraintIds": [
      "constraint-accessible-route"
    ],
    "includeSpatialEvidence": true
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.get_change_log",
  "input": {}
}
```

Use one exact Plan Version and preserve every returned fingerprint and stable ID.

## Verify history

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.replay_history",
  "input": {}
}
```

- The ledger hash chain must pass.
- The replayed current Plan fingerprint must match the stored fingerprint.
- The Approval actor must be human and authorized.
- Every waiver and Emergency Review must bind the approved Proposal and Validation fingerprint.

## Export the audit package

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.export_audit_package",
  "input": {}
}
```

Store the package checksum with the review record. The export is read-only and cannot change the Plan.

## Completion criteria

- Ledger integrity and replay both pass.
- The accepted Plan Version, Validation, Approval, reviews, receipts, comments, and geometry fingerprints reconcile.
- No agent-authored Approval or fabricated waiver exists.

## Verify the workflow

Run the executable fixture from the repository root. Completion requires a zero exit code.

```bash
node --test tests/venue-planner.test.mjs tests/plan-exports.test.mjs tests/authorization.test.mjs
```

# Install the VenueMind MCP server

Build the standalone stdio server, connect one host, and open a durable Project-scoped session.

## Build the server

```bash
npm install
npm run build:mcp
```

## Configure Codex

```bash
mkdir -p ./venuemind-data
codex mcp add venuemind --env VENUEMIND_DATA_DIR=$PWD/venuemind-data -- node $PWD/packages/mcp-server/dist/index.js
codex mcp get venuemind
```

Other stdio hosts use the same command, arguments, and explicit writable data directory.

## Open a Project session

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.list_projects",
  "input": {}
}
```

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.open_project",
  "input": {
    "projectId": "project-summit-forward"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.inspect_layout",
  "input": {}
}
```

## Completion criteria

- The host lists all 39 tool contracts at version 1.2.0.
- The active session is bound to one Project.
- Project state survives a server restart.
- Approval remains absent from the tool list.

## Other clients

- [MCP client configurations](/docs/mcp#desktop-hosts)

## Verify the workflow

Run the executable fixture from the repository root. Completion requires a zero exit code.

```bash
node --test tests/mcp-server.test.mjs
```

# Use VenueMind through native WebMCP

Expose the active Studio as a scoped browser tool surface and complete a safe read-to-Proposal workflow.

## Open the native surface

1. Start the VenueMind development server.
2. Open /studio/project-summit-forward in a WebMCP-capable browser host.
3. Open WebMCP diagnostics and confirm READY, contract 1.2.0, and 39 registered tools.

## Invoke through the browser

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.inspect_layout",
  "input": {}
}
```

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.preview_revision",
  "input": {
    "goal": "Protect the west accessible route and reduce entrance congestion",
    "idempotencyKey": "tutorial-webmcp-preview-001",
    "correlationId": "tutorial-webmcp-001"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.validate_layout",
  "input": {}
}
```

## Observe the shared state

- The Studio displays the same Proposal and violet ghost Changes returned to the caller.
- Tool results contain bounded structured content plus a compact summary.
- The call correlation and idempotency metadata appear in receipts and the Activity Ledger.
- Reloading the page unregisters and safely registers the tool suite again.

## Completion criteria

- Read and Proposal calls succeed within their Agent Grant scopes.
- Missing scope, oversized input, cancellation, and stale state return stable error envelopes.
- The agent cannot approve or delete a Project.

## Verify the workflow

Run the executable fixture from the repository root. Completion requires a zero exit code.

```bash
node --test tests/webmcp-conformance.test.mjs
```

# Install and invoke VenueMind agent skills

Build six versioned skill packages and invoke the smallest workflow-specific skill for the task.

## Build and inspect

```bash
npm run build:skills
npm run validate:skills
node -e "const m=require('./dist/skills/manifest.json'); console.log(m.packages.map(p => p.name+'@'+p.version).join('\n'))"
```

Install the desired directory from dist/skills into the skill location used by the agent host.

## Choose one skill

- venuemind-plan — supervised planning and Proposal branches.
- venuemind-audit — evidence, authority, ledger, and replay.
- venuemind-access-review — accessible routes, seating, doors, ramps, and sightlines.
- venuemind-crowd-flow — deterministic Scenario comparison and queue evidence.
- venuemind-production-plan — AV, staging, power, rigging, cable, and service routes.
- venuemind-event-day — live issue triage and supervised adjustments.

## Invoke with a bounded outcome

```text
Use $venuemind-access-review to inspect the active Proposal, explain every failed accessibility Constraint by stable ID, and prepare one validated remediation branch. Stop at human review.
```

## Completion criteria

- The installed package version and tool contract version match the manifest.
- The skill loads generated schema references only when its workflow needs them.
- Required evidence is present and unnecessary referenced calls remain absent.
- The skill stops at human Approval.

## Verify the workflow

Run the executable fixture from the repository root. Completion requires a zero exit code.

```bash
node --test tests/skills.test.mjs
```

# Import, validate, and export a venue plan

Preview an Interchange Package, commit it as a new Project, validate exact geometry, and produce portable exports.

## Preview before import

1. Open /projects and select IMPORT.
2. Choose public/examples/venuemind-project-package.json from the repository.
3. Review the package ID, checksum, migration report, stable-ID checks, geometry checks, Lock checks, ledger integrity, and replay status.
4. Confirm the Project ID does not already exist.

## Commit and validate

1. Select IMPORT PROJECT only when the preview status is ready.
2. Open the created Project.
3. Run venue.inspect_layout and venue.validate_layout.
4. Reconcile the candidate geometry and Validation fingerprints with the import preview.

## Export portable evidence

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.export_plan",
  "input": {
    "format": "package"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.export_plan",
  "input": {
    "format": "pdf"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "tool": "venue.export_audit_package",
  "input": {}
}
```

- Use VM JSON for authoritative round-trip interchange.
- Use PDF or layered SVG for human review.
- Use the audit package for ledger, replay, and evidence verification.

## Completion criteria

- Import never overwrites an existing Project ID.
- The clean installation reproduces the same Plan, Constraint, version, and ledger fingerprints.
- Every export identifies the evaluated Plan Version and Validation evidence.

## Verify the workflow

Run the executable fixture from the repository root. Completion requires a zero exit code.

```bash
node --test tests/interchange.test.mjs tests/plan-exports.test.mjs
```

# Recover from offline local state

Preserve Project work when the remote Project endpoint is unavailable and reconcile it without silent data loss.

## Seed the recovery cache

1. Open a Project while the Project API is available.
2. Confirm the Studio save indicator reports REMOTE.
3. Make one Proposal-safe change and wait for the remote save.
4. The browser now holds a recovery copy under the Project-scoped storage key.

## Continue during an API outage

1. Block requests matching /api/projects while keeping the application assets available.
2. Create or adjust a Proposal Change.
3. Confirm the save indicator reports LOCAL.
4. Navigate to /projects and confirm the cached Project remains discoverable with its complete snapshot.

## Recover deliberately

1. Restore the Project endpoint before accepting further shared changes.
2. Open the locally recovered Project and export VM JSON as a safety copy.
3. Compare its updated time, Plan Version, Proposal, and latest receipt with the remote record.
4. Preserve divergent work as a Proposal Branch; do not silently replace accepted remote truth.

## Completion criteria

- The local record retains schema version 10 and the exact Project snapshot.
- Remote failure is explicit through the LOCAL status.
- Recovery never changes accepted Plan truth without the ordinary Proposal, Validation, and human Approval path.

## Verify the workflow

Run the executable fixture from the repository root. Completion requires a zero exit code.

```bash
node --test tests/project-store.test.mjs
```

---

# WebMCP tools

The active VenueMind page exposes compact tools backed by the same command interface as the visible Studio.

## Runtime boundary

- Contract version 1.2.0 is attached to every published tool.
- Lifecycle states: detecting, registering, ready, failed, unsupported, unregistered.
- Every invocation returns a compact text summary and versioned structured content.
- Mutation receipts retain caller idempotency and correlation metadata.
- Authorization scopes: venue:read, venue:propose, venue:comment, venue:simulate, venue:export.
- Input and output byte limits are published per tool and enforced before data crosses the boundary.
- Sensitive credentials, contact fields, and attendee-record keys are redacted from structured results.
- Abort signals unregister the page tool suite and cancel active calls where the invoking browser supplies a call signal.

## Generated catalog

Each native browser tool has one canonical reference page shared with the standalone MCP surface.

- [Browse all tool contracts](/docs/reference-tools)

---

# MCP server

A durable, session-scoped stdio server built on the official Model Context Protocol TypeScript SDK v2.

## Build and launch

```bash
npm run build:mcp
node /absolute/path/to/venue-mind/packages/mcp-server/dist/index.js
```

## Durable Project sessions

- Filesystem repository with atomic writes.
- One active Project per MCP connection.
- venue.list_projects and venue.open_project select Project scope.
- Set VENUEMIND_DATA_DIR to an explicit writable data directory.
- Project record schema version 10.

## Protocol surfaces

- 39 tools generated from one shared contract source across WebMCP and standalone MCP.
- Current Project, Plan Version, Proposal, schema, documentation, and compatibility resources.
- Project and Plan Version resource templates with completion.
- Supervised planning and Plan audit prompts.
- Progress notifications for Validation and Simulation.
- Structured standard-error logs and graceful interruption handling.

## Codex

```bash
codex mcp add venuemind --env VENUEMIND_DATA_DIR=/absolute/path/to/venuemind-data -- node /absolute/path/to/venue-mind/packages/mcp-server/dist/index.js
codex mcp get venuemind
```

## Claude Desktop, Cursor, and generic clients

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "venuemind": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": [
        "/absolute/path/to/venue-mind/packages/mcp-server/dist/index.js"
      ],
      "env": {
        "VENUEMIND_DATA_DIR": "/absolute/path/to/venuemind-data"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

- Claude Desktop: add the entry to claude_desktop_config.json and restart.
- Cursor: save it as .cursor/mcp.json for Project scope or ~/.cursor/mcp.json for global scope.
- Generic local MCP hosts commonly accept the same process configuration.

## Official MCP Inspector

```bash
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector node /absolute/path/to/venue-mind/packages/mcp-server/dist/index.js
```

## ChatGPT-compatible remote deployment

ChatGPT custom MCP apps connect to remote endpoints, not directly to a local stdio process. Put an authenticated Streamable HTTP Adapter or supported secure MCP tunnel in front of the same server Module; never expose the stdio process itself to the network.

- Validate OAuth tokens and token audience.
- Publish protected-resource metadata.
- Bind Project access to the authenticated principal.
- Enforce VenueMind authorization scopes.
- Use TLS, restrict origins, and reject caller-supplied organization or actor authority.

## Compatibility

- MCP server 0.4.0.
- Preferred protocol revision 2026-07-28.
- Minimum supported revision 2025-03-26.
- Tool contract 1.2.0.
- Approval authority: human-only.

## Human-only approval

The MCP surface can inspect, preview, validate, branch, switch, read, and export. Approval is deliberately absent; the VenueMind Studio owns the human commit decision.

---

# Agent skills

Six versioned skill packages teach supervised VenueMind workflows against tool contract 1.2.0.

## venuemind-plan

Prepare seating, access, circulation, sightline, production, catering, capacity, and queue Proposal branches. Stops at human review.

```text
Use $venuemind-plan to create and validate an access-first Proposal branch.
```

## venuemind-audit

Reconcile Plan Versions, Constraints, Validation fingerprints, Locks, receipts, approval authorship, and Activity Ledger replay.

```text
Use $venuemind-audit to inspect this Plan for stale branches and missing evidence.
```

## venuemind-access-review

Review routes, doors, ramps, accessible and companion seating, turning space, and access sightlines. It reports policy provenance without claiming legal certification.

```text
Use $venuemind-access-review to explain this failed route and prepare a remediation branch.
```

## venuemind-crowd-flow

Run seeded ingress, interval, egress, emergency, queue, and bottleneck scenarios while keeping simulation evidence separate from deterministic Validation.

```text
Use $venuemind-crowd-flow to compare these two egress strategies.
```

## venuemind-production-plan

Plan staging, AV, power points, cable routes, production access, and service lanes while checking audience impacts.

```text
Use $venuemind-production-plan to prepare a validated production branch.
```

## venuemind-event-day

Triage live issues with stable incident anchors, current-plan evidence, simulations, and supervised Adjustment Requests.

```text
Use $venuemind-event-day to triage this live queue obstruction.
```

## Authority boundary

- No skill can accept a Proposal or delete a Project.
- No skill may override effective Locks or manufacture a Warning Waiver.
- Stale versions, incompatible simulation fingerprints, and missing evidence remain explicit failures.
- Emergency response remains with venue operators and local emergency services.

## Build and install

```bash
npm run build:skills
cp -R /absolute/path/to/venue-mind/dist/skills/venuemind-* /absolute/path/to/codex-skills/
```

- [Skill package manifest](/skills-manifest.json)
- [Evaluation metrics](/skill-evaluation-metrics.json)

## Evaluation suite

- 12 normal and adversarial workflow cases.
- Premature Approval, ignored Locks, stale versions, and missing evidence fixtures.
- Required-tool selection accuracy: 100%.
- Unnecessary referenced-call rate: 0%.
- Every case requires stable evidence and stops at human Approval.

# Client examples

Validated WebMCP, MCP, Codex, Claude Desktop, Cursor, JSON-RPC, retry, failure, and export examples.

## Browser WebMCP

The open Studio registers native tools. The browser agent host invokes them; the published harness captures the same registrations for deterministic local execution.

```javascript
// The browser host invokes tools registered by the open VenueMind page.
const result = await harness.invoke("venue.preview_revision", {
  goal: "Protect the west accessible route",
  idempotencyKey: "browser-example-preview-001",
  correlationId: "browser-example-001",
});
if (result.isError) throw new Error(result.structuredContent.error.code);

```

- [Executable browser harness](/examples/client/webmcp/browser-invocation.mjs)
- [WebMCP tutorial](/docs/tutorial-webmcp)

## Generic stdio client

```json
{
  "transport": "stdio",
  "command": "node",
  "args": [
    "<VENUE_MIND_ROOT>/packages/mcp-server/dist/index.js"
  ],
  "env": {
    "VENUEMIND_DATA_DIR": "<WRITABLE_DATA_DIR>",
    "VENUEMIND_ORGANIZATION_ID": "<ORGANIZATION_ID>"
  }
}
```

- Replace <VENUE_MIND_ROOT> with the absolute repository path.
- Replace <WRITABLE_DATA_DIR> with a dedicated writable directory.
- The host launches one local server process per stdio session.
- Standard output is protocol-only; structured diagnostics use standard error.

- [Generic configuration](/examples/client/config/generic-stdio.json)
- [Executable TypeScript client](/examples/client/typescript/supervised-workflow.ts)
- [Official MCP TypeScript client guide](https://ts.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io/v2/clients/connect)

## Codex

```bash
codex mcp add venuemind --env VENUEMIND_DATA_DIR=<WRITABLE_DATA_DIR> -- node <VENUE_MIND_ROOT>/packages/mcp-server/dist/index.js
codex mcp get venuemind
```

```toml
[mcp_servers.venuemind]
command = "node"
args = ["<VENUE_MIND_ROOT>/packages/mcp-server/dist/index.js"]
env = { VENUEMIND_DATA_DIR = "<WRITABLE_DATA_DIR>", VENUEMIND_ORGANIZATION_ID = "<ORGANIZATION_ID>" }

```

```text
Use VenueMind to inspect Project project-summit-forward, prepare one access-first Proposal, validate it, report stable Change and Constraint IDs, export JSON, and stop for human Approval in the Studio.
```

- [Codex TOML](/examples/client/config/codex.toml)

## Claude Desktop

1. Open Claude Desktop developer settings and edit the local MCP configuration.
2. Merge the venuemind entry under mcpServers.
3. Replace both path placeholders and restart Claude Desktop.
4. Confirm VenueMind tools are available before running the supervised prompt.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "venuemind": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": [
        "<VENUE_MIND_ROOT>/packages/mcp-server/dist/index.js"
      ],
      "env": {
        "VENUEMIND_DATA_DIR": "<WRITABLE_DATA_DIR>",
        "VENUEMIND_ORGANIZATION_ID": "<ORGANIZATION_ID>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```text
Open project-summit-forward in VenueMind. Inspect accepted truth, preview a revision that protects the west accessible route, validate it, explain every non-pass result, and stop for human Approval.
```

- [Claude Desktop configuration](/examples/client/config/claude-desktop.json)
- [Anthropic MCP documentation](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/mcp)

## Cursor

1. Create .cursor/mcp.json for Project scope or ~/.cursor/mcp.json for global scope.
2. Copy the configuration and replace both path placeholders.
3. Open Cursor MCP settings and confirm venuemind is enabled.
4. Keep tool approval enabled for the supervised workflow.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "venuemind": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": [
        "<VENUE_MIND_ROOT>/packages/mcp-server/dist/index.js"
      ],
      "env": {
        "VENUEMIND_DATA_DIR": "<WRITABLE_DATA_DIR>",
        "VENUEMIND_ORGANIZATION_ID": "<ORGANIZATION_ID>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```text
Using the VenueMind MCP tools, audit the current Plan, create a separate circulation-first Proposal Branch, validate it, compare it with the active Branch, and leave the decision to a human reviewer.
```

- [Cursor Project configuration](/examples/client/config/cursor-project.json)
- [Cursor MCP documentation](https://docs.cursor.com/context/model-context-protocol)

## Retry and failure workflows

- Exact retry — reuse one idempotency key only for byte-equivalent intent; VenueMind returns the original receipt.
- Stale base — retain PLAN_VERSION_CONFLICT details, inspect current truth, detect conflicts, then rebase the Proposal.
- Validation failure — use affected stable IDs and remediation evidence; create another Proposal revision and validate again.
- Export — export only the currently evaluated Plan or Proposal and retain its version, Validation ID, and evidence fingerprints.

- [Retry sequence](/examples/client/raw/retry-sequence.json)
- [Stale-base error](/examples/client/raw/stale-base.error.json)
- [Validation failure](/examples/client/raw/validation-failure.response.json)
- [Text export response](/examples/client/raw/export-text.response.json)

## Raw request and response fixtures

- [Preview request](/examples/client/raw/preview-revision.request.json)
- [Preview response](/examples/client/raw/preview-revision.response.json)
- [Example manifest](/examples/client/manifest.json)

Generation uses the production planner, error catalog, export implementation, and shared tool contracts. CI compiles and executes both code examples and contract-validates every configuration and fixture.

# Error catalog

Every stable VenueMind error code, user-safe message, and actionable remediation path.

## Published errors

| Code | Message | Remediation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| COMMAND_INVALID | Venue command requires a type. | Send one published Venue command with its required fields. |
| COMMAND_UNSUPPORTED | Venue command is not supported. | Refresh the command contract and use a published command type. |
| IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED | Idempotency key is required for mutating commands. | Retry with one stable idempotency key for this semantic action. |
| IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT | Idempotency key conflict. | Use the original command input or generate a new idempotency key. |
| SNAPSHOT_INVALID | Invalid VenueMind snapshot. | Restore a schema-compatible snapshot containing a Plan, Proposal, and Activity Ledger. |
| ADJUSTMENT_REQUIRED | Adjustment instruction is required. | Provide a concise operational adjustment. |
| PROPOSAL_NOT_REVIEWABLE | Only a Proposal under review can be changed. | Create or activate a Proposal with review status before changing it. |
| PROPOSAL_MISMATCH | Proposal ID does not match the active Proposal. | Inspect the active Proposal and retry with its stable ID. |
| BRANCH_NAME_REQUIRED | Proposal Branch name is required. | Provide a non-empty Branch name. |
| BRANCH_NOT_FOUND | Proposal Branch not found. | List Proposal Branches and retry with an existing stable Branch ID. |
| REBASE_CONFLICT | Unresolved Proposal conflicts block rebase. | Resolve blocking conflicts, then retry the rebase. |
| CONFLICT_NOT_FOUND | Proposal conflict not found. | Detect current Proposal conflicts and retry with a stable conflict ID. |
| CONFLICT_RESOLUTION_INVALID | Conflict resolution is not valid for this conflict. | Choose one of the conflict's published resolution options. |
| CONFLICT_HUMAN_REQUIRED | Only a human can resolve a Proposal conflict. | Ask an authorized human operator to choose a conflict outcome in VenueMind Studio. |
| LOCK_CONFLICT | Proposal Change conflicts with an active Lock. | Remove the locked property mutation or have a human release the applicable Project Lock. |
| LOCK_HUMAN_REQUIRED | Only a human can manage Project Locks. | Ask an authorized human operator to add or release the Project Lock. |
| LOCK_OBJECT_NOT_FOUND | Lock target object not found. | Inspect stable object IDs and retry with an object in the active Plan. |
| LOCK_TYPE_INVALID | Lock type is invalid. | Use position, rotation, dimension, deletion, or role. |
| LOCK_NOT_FOUND | Project Lock not found. | Inspect Project Locks and retry with an active stable Lock ID. |
| PLAN_VERSION_CONFLICT | Plan version conflict. | Inspect the latest Plan Version and create or rebase the Proposal before retrying. |
| VALIDATION_FAILED | Proposal validation failed. | Resolve every hard Constraint failure and validate again. |
| WARNING_WAIVER_REQUIRED | Proposal has warnings that require a human Warning Waiver. | Have a human record a reason-coded waiver for every open warning. |
| EMERGENCY_REVIEW_REQUIRED | Emergency Plan Change requires an authorized human Emergency Review. | Supply a reviewer ID, authorized reviewer role, and explicit assumption acceptance in VenueMind Studio. |
| EMERGENCY_REVIEW_UNAUTHORIZED | Emergency reviewer role is not authorized. | Use a reviewer assigned to one of the Emergency Plan's authorized reviewer roles. |
| WAIVER_HUMAN_REQUIRED | Only a human can create a Warning Waiver. | Ask an authorized human operator to record the disposition in VenueMind Studio. |
| WAIVER_AUTHOR_REQUIRED | Warning Waiver requires an author ID. | Supply the authenticated or local operator identity. |
| WAIVER_REASON_INVALID | Warning Waiver requires a supported reason code. | Choose one reason code from the Warning Waiver contract. |
| WARNING_NOT_WAIVABLE | Constraint does not have a waivable warning. | Validate again and select an open warning Constraint. |
| WARNING_ALREADY_WAIVED | Warning is already waived. | Use the existing Warning Waiver or revise the Proposal before recording another disposition. |
| CONSTRAINT_NOT_FOUND | Constraint not found. | Inspect the Plan and retry with an existing stable Constraint ID. |
| CONSTRAINT_INVALID | Constraint metadata is invalid. | Conform the Constraint to the published schema and retry. |
| CONSTRAINT_DUPLICATE | Constraint ID is duplicated. | Assign a unique stable ID to every Constraint. |
| CONSTRAINT_EVIDENCE_INVALID | Constraint evidence is invalid. | Provide numeric evidence and threshold values required by the evaluator. |
| CONSTRAINT_EVALUATOR_UNSUPPORTED | Constraint evaluator is not supported. | Use an evaluator published in the Venue Constraint schema. |
| GEOMETRY_INVALID | Spatial geometry is invalid. | Correct the reported boundary, Footprint, unit, or operational metadata and validate again. |
| SPATIAL_CHANGE_TARGET_MISSING | Spatial Change targets a missing object. | Inspect stable object IDs and rebuild the Change against the active Plan. |
| SPATIAL_CHANGE_TARGET_EXISTS | Spatial Change would reuse an existing object ID. | Create a new Project-scoped stable object ID and retry the placement. |
| SPATIAL_CHANGE_UNSUPPORTED | Spatial Change operation is not supported. | Use a published spatial Change operation. |
| TEMPLATE_VERSION_NOT_FOUND | Template version not found. | List the template catalog and select a published template ID and version. |
| TEMPLATE_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED | Template schema version is not supported. | Migrate the template document with a published migration path. |
| TEMPLATE_BINDING_NOT_FOUND | Project is not bound to this template. | Inspect the Project Template Binding and retry with its Room Template ID. |
| TEMPLATE_VERSION_CURRENT | Project already uses this template version. | Select a newer published Room Template version. |
| COMMENT_INVALID | Comment metadata is invalid. | Provide a non-empty comment body, supported status, and published fields. |
| COMMENT_ANCHOR_INVALID | Comment anchor does not resolve to an immutable VenueMind subject. | Inspect stable Project, Plan Version, Proposal, Change, Constraint, or coordinate identifiers and retry. |
| COMMENT_AUTHOR_REQUIRED | Comment action requires an author ID. | Supply the authenticated or local author identity. |
| COMMENT_NOT_FOUND | Comment not found. | List comments and retry with an existing stable Comment ID. |
| PROJECT_NOT_FOUND | Project not found. | List Projects and retry with an existing stable Project ID. |
| PROJECT_TOOL_UNAVAILABLE | Project tools are unavailable in this session. | Open VenueMind from a Project-aware host and retry the Project operation. |
| OBJECT_NOT_FOUND | Venue object not found. | Search objects and retry with an existing stable object ID. |
| VALIDATION_NOT_FOUND | Validation result not found. | Validate the current Proposal and retry with its Validation ID. |
| SCENARIO_RUN_NOT_FOUND | Scenario Run not found. | List Scenario Runs and retry with an existing stable Run ID. |
| TOOL_SCOPE_REQUIRED | Tool authorization scope is required. | Grant the published scope for this tool or use a read-only tool within the current session. |
| AUTHORIZATION_DENIED | The current principal is not authorized for this VenueMind action. | Use an assigned Organization Membership Role or an active Organization- and Project-scoped Agent Grant containing the required permission. |
| AGENT_GRANT_INVALID | Agent Grant is invalid. | Issue a complete Organization- and Project-scoped grant with published scopes and a lifetime of one hour or less. |
| TOOL_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE | Tool payload exceeds its published size limit. | Reduce the requested geometry or export payload and retry within the published byte limit. |
| TOOL_CALL_CANCELLED | Tool call was cancelled. | Retry only if the caller still needs the operation, using the same idempotency key for an interrupted mutation. |
| LEDGER_INTEGRITY_FAILED | Activity Ledger integrity failed. | Restore an untampered snapshot or recover the last verified Project record. |
| VENUE_INTERNAL_ERROR | VenueMind could not complete the operation. | Retry once; if the error persists, inspect the server log with the correlation ID. |

## Error envelope

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "PLAN_VERSION_CONFLICT",
    "message": "Plan version conflict.",
    "remediation": "Inspect the latest Plan Version and create or rebase the Proposal before retrying.",
    "details": {
      "expectedVersion": "3.3",
      "receivedVersion": "3.2"
    }
  }
}
```

- [Venue error schema](/schemas/venue-error.schema.json)

# Constraint and evidence reference

All deterministic Constraint evaluators, operational categories, evidence families, and normalized units.

## Evaluators

| Evaluator | Category | Evidence | Units |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| minimum_metric | configured metric | actual, threshold, comparator | Constraint parameter unit |
| maximum_metric | configured metric | actual, threshold, comparator | Constraint parameter unit |
| protected_objects_unchanged | protection | changed and protected object IDs | count |
| accessible_route_graph | accessibility | reachable destinations, path widths, route edges | m, count |
| turning_clearance | accessibility | destination clearance diameters | m |
| accessible_seating | accessibility | seat count, section distribution, companion adjacency | seats, sections, ratio |
| accessible_seating_sightlines | accessibility | sampled accessible-seat rays and section coverage | ratio, m, degrees |
| door_clearance | accessibility | door clear width and obstruction IDs | m, count |
| temporary_ramp | accessibility | rise, run, slope, width, landing, edge protection, handrails | ratio, m, boolean |
| occupancy_capacity | capacity | placed, usable-area, section, zone, venue, and operational load | attendees, m², ratio |
| circulation_graph | circulation | paths, clear widths, exit approaches, bottlenecks, phase loads | m, persons, persons/min, index |
| sightline_raycast | sightlines | sampled rays, viewing angles, distance, obstruction IDs | ratio, m, degrees |
| production_readiness | production | throw, visibility, sound, cameras, control, cable, power, rigging, inventory | m, degrees, W, kg, count |
| catering_readiness | catering | phase capacity, queue spill, separation, access, replenishment, inventory | persons/min, persons, m, ratio, count |
| emergency_readiness | emergency | exit capacity, routes, assembly, responder access, equipment, backup power | persons, persons/min, m, min, count |

## Outcomes and authority

- pass — measured evidence meets the threshold.
- warning — reviewable evidence requires an explicit human Warning Waiver when waivable.
- fail — a hard safety or operational threshold blocks Approval.
- not-applicable — the evaluator records why the current scope has no applicable target.
- Simulation Results remain separate from deterministic Constraint evidence.

## Schemas

- [Constraint schema](/schemas/venue-constraint.schema.json)
- [Validation result schema](/schemas/validation-result.schema.json)
- [Spatial evidence schema](/schemas/spatial-evidence.schema.json)

## Integrity and replay

- Every entry carries a sequence, previous hash, content hash, actor identity, source, session, and timestamp.
- Load and export verify the complete chain from genesis.
- Replay applies accepted Plan transitions and compares the reconstructed fingerprint with stored current truth.
- A failed chain or Lock-protected replay is blocking.

- [Activity Ledger schema](/schemas/activity-ledger.schema.json)
- [Audit tutorial](/docs/tutorial-audit-plan)

---

# Plan and Proposal lifecycle

Branch, rebase, conflict, Approval, adjustment, undo, redo, and replay behavior at the shared command boundary.

## Accepted truth

- One immutable Plan Version is accepted truth.
- A Proposal names exactly one base Plan Version and contains stable Changes.
- Branches isolate competing Proposal revisions; switching a Branch never changes the accepted Plan.

## Rebase and conflicts

- Conflict detection covers stale base, deleted dependency, Lock, same-object edit, geometry overlap, and Constraint regression.
- Rebase retains unchanged Change IDs and creates new IDs only for transformed Changes.
- Human conflict decisions use only the published outcomes for each conflict and trigger fresh Validation.

## Approval

- Approval requires a matching Proposal ID and base version, passing hard Constraints, warning dispositions, and any required Emergency Review.
- Approval is human-only and creates exactly one immutable Plan Version plus one ledger transition.
- Agent tools stop at validated human review.

## Undo, redo, and replay

- Proposal editing undo and redo create reviewable Proposal revisions.
- Accepted Plan undo and redo restore immutable prior versions and append ledger transitions.
- Replay reconstructs accepted history without trusting cached summary fields.

## Related contracts

- [Proposal conflicts](/schemas/proposal-conflicts.schema.json)
- [Proposal comparison](/schemas/proposal-comparison.schema.json)
- [Command receipt](/schemas/command-receipt.schema.json)

---

# Persistence and recovery

Remote authority, browser recovery, import safety, soft deletion, normalization, and integrity behavior.

## Storage semantics

| Concern | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Authoritative state | The Project repository is authoritative when reachable; every accepted snapshot is stored with schema version 10. |
| Recovery cache | The browser writes a Project-scoped local copy before each remote save and reports LOCAL when the endpoint is unavailable. |
| Record revision | Every authoritative Project record has a server-assigned positive revision and strong ETag. Existing writes require the exact current If-Match value. |
| Reconciliation | Base/local/remote comparison merges independent fields once. Overlapping planning state returns PROJECT_REVISION_CONFLICT and remains unsynchronized. |
| Planning recovery | The local Proposal is retained in Organization-scoped recovery storage and can become an auditable Recovery Branch on current remote truth. |
| Reload | A remote record refreshes the recovery copy; a missing or unavailable endpoint may load the local Project-scoped record. |
| Import | Import is create-only. An existing local or remote Project ID returns PROJECT_ID_CONFLICT. |
| Deletion | Soft deletion records deletedAt and recoveryUntil; restoration remains available for seven days. |
| Integrity | Schema normalization, geometry validation, Lock checks, ledger verification, and replay precede authoritative use. |

## Optimistic concurrency

- Creation requires If-None-Match: *; updates require the exact strong Project ETag in If-Match.
- A stale write returns PROJECT_REVISION_CONFLICT with current record and revision data; it never falls back to a successful LOCAL state.
- Independent fields reconcile through one bounded three-way retry. Overlapping layout state becomes a human-controlled Recovery Branch or yields to REMOTE.

- [Concurrency guide](/guides/optimistic-concurrency.md)

## Real-time collaboration

- Presence Leases carry User identity, observed Plan Version, and focused stable object for 30 seconds.
- SSE resumes from a durable per-Project cursor and streams Comment, ledger, Proposal, Approval, and record events.
- A missing cursor link emits sync.reset and reloads authoritative Project state through ordinary revision conflict rules.

- [Collaboration guide](/guides/realtime-collaboration.md)

## Recovery workflow

- [Offline recovery tutorial](/docs/tutorial-offline-recovery)
- [Interchange tutorial](/docs/tutorial-import-export)
- [Project record schema](/schemas/project-record.schema.json)

# Authorization reference

Human Roles, Agent Grant scopes, service-boundary permissions, and Approval authority from the published authorization policy.

## Human Roles

| Role | Permissions |
| --- | --- |
| viewer | project.read, plan.read, proposal.read, comment.read, simulation.read |
| planner | project.read, plan.read, proposal.read, comment.read, simulation.read, proposal.create, proposal.manage, comment.write, simulation.run, export.plan |
| reviewer | project.read, plan.read, proposal.read, comment.read, simulation.read, proposal.review, comment.write, export.audit, audit.read |
| approver | project.read, plan.read, proposal.read, comment.read, simulation.read, proposal.review, comment.write, export.audit, audit.read, approval.approve, approval.waive |
| venue-administrator | project.read, plan.read, proposal.read, comment.read, simulation.read, proposal.create, proposal.manage, comment.write, simulation.run, export.plan, proposal.review, export.audit, audit.read, approval.approve, approval.waive, project.manage, plan.update, lock.manage |
| organization-administrator | project.read, project.manage, plan.read, plan.update, proposal.read, proposal.create, proposal.manage, proposal.review, comment.read, comment.write, simulation.read, simulation.run, export.plan, export.audit, audit.read, approval.approve, approval.waive, lock.manage |

## Agent Grant scopes

| Scope | Permissions |
| --- | --- |
| venue:read | project.read, plan.read, proposal.read, comment.read, simulation.read, audit.read |
| venue:propose | proposal.create, proposal.manage |
| venue:comment | comment.read, comment.write |
| venue:simulate | simulation.read, simulation.run |
| venue:export | export.plan, export.audit |

## Policy decisions

- Agent Grants bind one agent to one Organization and one Project for at most 60 minutes.
- Approval requires one of: approver, venue-administrator, organization-administrator.
- Approval, Warning Waivers, Project Locks, and conflict decisions remain human-only.
- Denied planner commands append sanitized authorization.denied evidence without retaining protected input payloads.

- [Published authorization policy](/authorization-policy.json)
- [Agent Grant schema](/schemas/agent-grant.schema.json)
- [Authentication and tenancy](/guides/authentication-and-tenancy.md)

# Compatibility and deprecation

Current public versions, comparison rules, migration guarantees, and the policy for changing stable surfaces.

## Compatibility matrix

| Surface | Current | Compatibility rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Project record | 10 | Migrates released snapshots from schema 5 through 10 before use. |
| Spatial geometry | 1 | Canonical metres with millimetre serialization precision. |
| Venue Template catalog | 1 | Schema-0 inventory stock migrates to availability metadata. |
| Validation engine | 2.7.0 | Comparable only when engine and immutable input fingerprints match. |
| Simulation engine | 1.2.1 | Comparison requires matching engine and Scenario definition fingerprints. |
| Activity Ledger | 1 | Hash-chain verification is required on load, replay, and export. |
| Tool contracts | 1.2.0 | Shared by WebMCP, standalone MCP, schemas, examples, and skills. |
| MCP server | 0.4.0 | Preferred protocol 2026-07-28; minimum 2025-03-26. |
| Agent skills | 1.1.0 | Targets tool contract 1.2.0. |
| Interchange Package | 1 | Create-only import with checksum, migration, geometry, ledger, and replay preflight. |

## Deprecation policy

| Change | Policy |
| --- | --- |
| Breaking contract or schema | Publish a new major contract or schema version with an explicit migration path; retain the prior published artifact. |
| Additive field or operation | Publish a minor tool-contract release and update generated schemas, examples, skills, and changelog together. |
| Clarification or remediation text | Publish a patch release when runtime behavior is unchanged. |
| Deprecated tool or field | Mark it in machine-readable metadata and the changelog for at least one full minor release before removal. |
| Stable identifier | Preserve it across revisions and migrations; create a new ID only when identity or transformed lineage changes. |

## Current status

- No public tool, command, schema field, or skill is currently deprecated.
- Every future deprecation is machine-readable, visible in the changelog, and covered by contract tests.

- Read-only operation.
- Input limit 65536 bytes; output limit 262144 bytes.

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Bounds | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |


```json
{}
```

## Output

Bounded Project summaries visible to the current Project-scoped grant.

| Output field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| source | Published result field. |
| projects[] | Published result field. |

- Stable ID: projects[].id
- Stable ID: projects[].activePlanId

## Errors

| Code | Message | Remediation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TOOL_SCOPE_REQUIRED | Tool authorization scope is required. | Grant the published scope for this tool or use a read-only tool within the current session. |
| AUTHORIZATION_DENIED | The current principal is not authorized for this VenueMind action. | Use an assigned Organization Membership Role or an active Organization- and Project-scoped Agent Grant containing the required permission. |
| AGENT_GRANT_INVALID | Agent Grant is invalid. | Issue a complete Organization- and Project-scoped grant with published scopes and a lifetime of one hour or less. |
| TOOL_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE | Tool payload exceeds its published size limit. | Reduce the requested geometry or export payload and retry within the published byte limit. |
| TOOL_CALL_CANCELLED | Tool call was cancelled. | Retry only if the caller still needs the operation, using the same idempotency key for an interrupted mutation. |
| VENUE_INTERNAL_ERROR | VenueMind could not complete the operation. | Retry once; if the error persists, inspect the server log with the correlation ID. |
| PROJECT_TOOL_UNAVAILABLE | Project tools are unavailable in this session. | Open VenueMind from a Project-aware host and retry the Project operation. |
| PROJECT_NOT_FOUND | Project not found. | List Projects and retry with an existing stable Project ID. |

## Surfaces

- [WebMCP runtime](/docs/webmcp#runtime)
- [Standalone MCP](/docs/mcp#surfaces)

# venue.search_objects

Search stable venue objects with bounded text, kind, layer, Lock, and accepted-versus-Proposal filters.

## Contract

- Contract version 1.2.0.
- Required Agent Grant scope venue:read.
- Read-only operation.
- Input limit 65536 bytes; output limit 262144 bytes.

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Bounds | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| query | string | no | — | max 200 chars | Published contract field. |
| kinds | string[] | no | — | max 10 items; unique items | Published contract field. |
| layers | architecture \| furniture \| access \| production \| catering \| safety \| annotations[] | no | — | max 7 items; unique items | Published contract field. |
| locked | boolean | no | — | — | Published contract field. |
| scope | accepted \| proposal | no | "proposal" | — | Accepted Plan or visible Proposal candidate. |
| limit | integer | no | 20 | ≥ 1; ≤ 50 | Maximum number of returned records. |

```json
{
  "query": "route",
  "layers": [
    "access"
  ],
  "limit": 10
}
```

## Output

A bounded object search result.

| Output field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| scope | Published result field. |
| planId | Stable identifier. |
| planVersion | Published result field. |
| proposalId | Stable identifier. |
| total | Published result field. |
| limit | Published result field. |
| truncated | Published result field. |
| objects[] | Published result field. |

- Stable ID: planId
- Stable ID: proposalId
- Stable ID: objects[].id

## Errors

| Code | Message | Remediation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TOOL_SCOPE_REQUIRED | Tool authorization scope is required. | Grant the published scope for this tool or use a read-only tool within the current session. |
| AUTHORIZATION_DENIED | The current principal is not authorized for this VenueMind action. | Use an assigned Organization Membership Role or an active Organization- and Project-scoped Agent Grant containing the required permission. |
| AGENT_GRANT_INVALID | Agent Grant is invalid. | Issue a complete Organization- and Project-scoped grant with published scopes and a lifetime of one hour or less. |
| TOOL_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE | Tool payload exceeds its published size limit. | Reduce the requested geometry or export payload and retry within the published byte limit. |
| TOOL_CALL_CANCELLED | Tool call was cancelled. | Retry only if the caller still needs the operation, using the same idempotency key for an interrupted mutation. |
| VENUE_INTERNAL_ERROR | VenueMind could not complete the operation. | Retry once; if the error persists, inspect the server log with the correlation ID. |

## Surfaces

- [WebMCP runtime](/docs/webmcp#runtime)
- [Standalone MCP](/docs/mcp#surfaces)
- [Complete error catalog](/docs/reference-errors)

# venue.preview_revision

Create a non-destructive venue revision preview. The result remains pending until a human approves it in VenueMind.

## Contract

- Contract version 1.2.0.
- Required Agent Grant scope venue:propose.
- State-affecting operation.
- Input limit 65536 bytes; output limit 262144 bytes.

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Bounds | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| goal | string | yes | — | min 1 chars | The spatial outcome the revision should achieve. |
| idempotencyKey | string | yes | — | min 1 chars | Unique retry key for this semantic command. |
| correlationId | string | no | — | min 1 chars | Optional caller correlation identifier. |

```json
{
  "goal": "Reduce entrance congestion",
  "idempotencyKey": "example-preview-001",
  "correlationId": "example-001"
}
```

## Output

A non-destructive Proposal revision; accepted Plan truth is unchanged.

| Output field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| proposalId | Stable identifier. |
| baseVersion | Published result field. |
| revision | Published result field. |
| changedItems | Published result field. |
| requiresHumanApproval | Published result field. |
| receipt | Published result field. |

- Stable ID: proposalId
- Stable ID: receipt.id
- Stable ID: receipt.resultIds.changeId

## Errors

| Code | Message | Remediation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TOOL_SCOPE_REQUIRED | Tool authorization scope is required. | Grant the published scope for this tool or use a read-only tool within the current session. |
| AUTHORIZATION_DENIED | The current principal is not authorized for this VenueMind action. | Use an assigned Organization Membership Role or an active Organization- and Project-scoped Agent Grant containing the required permission. |
| AGENT_GRANT_INVALID | Agent Grant is invalid. | Issue a complete Organization- and Project-scoped grant with published scopes and a lifetime of one hour or less. |
| TOOL_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE | Tool payload exceeds its published size limit. | Reduce the requested geometry or export payload and retry within the published byte limit. |
| TOOL_CALL_CANCELLED | Tool call was cancelled. | Retry only if the caller still needs the operation, using the same idempotency key for an interrupted mutation. |
| VENUE_INTERNAL_ERROR | VenueMind could not complete the operation. | Retry once; if the error persists, inspect the server log with the correlation ID. |
| IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED | Idempotency key is required for mutating commands. | Retry with one stable idempotency key for this semantic action. |
| IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT | Idempotency key conflict. | Use the original command input or generate a new idempotency key. |

## Surfaces

- [WebMCP runtime](/docs/webmcp#runtime)
- [Standalone MCP](/docs/mcp#surfaces)
- [Complete error catalog](/docs/reference-errors)

- Stable ID: branchId
- Stable ID: proposalId
- Stable ID: receipt.id

## Errors

| Code | Message | Remediation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TOOL_SCOPE_REQUIRED | Tool authorization scope is required. | Grant the published scope for this tool or use a read-only tool within the current session. |
| AUTHORIZATION_DENIED | The current principal is not authorized for this VenueMind action. | Use an assigned Organization Membership Role or an active Organization- and Project-scoped Agent Grant containing the required permission. |
| AGENT_GRANT_INVALID | Agent Grant is invalid. | Issue a complete Organization- and Project-scoped grant with published scopes and a lifetime of one hour or less. |
| TOOL_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE | Tool payload exceeds its published size limit. | Reduce the requested geometry or export payload and retry within the published byte limit. |
| TOOL_CALL_CANCELLED | Tool call was cancelled. | Retry only if the caller still needs the operation, using the same idempotency key for an interrupted mutation. |
| VENUE_INTERNAL_ERROR | VenueMind could not complete the operation. | Retry once; if the error persists, inspect the server log with the correlation ID. |
| IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED | Idempotency key is required for mutating commands. | Retry with one stable idempotency key for this semantic action. |
| IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT | Idempotency key conflict. | Use the original command input or generate a new idempotency key. |

## Surfaces

- [WebMCP runtime](/docs/webmcp#runtime)
- [Standalone MCP](/docs/mcp#surfaces)
- [Complete error catalog](/docs/reference-errors)

| IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT | Idempotency key conflict. | Use the original command input or generate a new idempotency key. |

# venue.run_scenario

Run one seeded operations, ingress-egress, or spatial queue Scenario against an exact Proposal Branch geometry. Results never replace deterministic Validation.

## Contract

- Contract version 1.2.0.
- Required Agent Grant scope venue:simulate.
- State-affecting operation.
- Input limit 131072 bytes; output limit 262144 bytes.

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Bounds | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| scenario | object | yes | — | — | Published contract field. |
| branchId | string | no | — | min 1 chars | Stable Proposal Branch ID. |
| idempotencyKey | string | yes | — | min 1 chars | Unique retry key for this semantic command. |
| correlationId | string | no | — | min 1 chars | Optional caller correlation identifier. |

```json
{
  "scenario": {
    "id": "scenario-example",
    "name": "Arrival peak",
    "seed": 42,
    "horizonSeconds": 1800,
    "sampleCount": 32,
    "inputs": {
      "population": 400,
      "arrivalRatePerMinute": 30,
      "serviceRatePerMinute": 10,
      "servers": 3
    }
  },
  "branchId": "branch-balanced",
  "idempotencyKey": "example-scenario-001"
}
```

## Output

A deterministic-seed Simulation Run; it never becomes Constraint Validation.

| Output field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| status | Published result field. |
| runId | Stable identifier. |
| scenarioId | Stable identifier. |
| branchId | Stable identifier. |
| inputFingerprint | Published result field. |
| cacheHit | Published result field. |
| result | Published result field. |
| receipt | Published result field. |

- Stable ID: runId
- Stable ID: scenarioId
- Stable ID: branchId
- Stable ID: receipt.id

## Errors

| Code | Message | Remediation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TOOL_SCOPE_REQUIRED | Tool authorization scope is required. | Grant the published scope for this tool or use a read-only tool within the current session. |
| AUTHORIZATION_DENIED | The current principal is not authorized for this VenueMind action. | Use an assigned Organization Membership Role or an active Organization- and Project-scoped Agent Grant containing the required permission. |
| AGENT_GRANT_INVALID | Agent Grant is invalid. | Issue a complete Organization- and Project-scoped grant with published scopes and a lifetime of one hour or less. |
| TOOL_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE | Tool payload exceeds its published size limit. | Reduce the requested geometry or export payload and retry within the published byte limit. |
| TOOL_CALL_CANCELLED | Tool call was cancelled. | Retry only if the caller still needs the operation, using the same idempotency key for an interrupted mutation. |

# run_scenario

Execute Run Scenario through the shared VenueMind planner boundary.

## Contract

- Permission simulation.run.
- Retry-safe mutation with a required idempotency key.
- Authority is evaluated at the service boundary.

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Bounds | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| type | const "run_scenario" | yes | — | — | Stable command discriminator. |
| scenario | object | yes | — | — | Published contract field. |
| branchId | string | no | — | min 1 chars | Stable Proposal Branch ID. |
| actor | human \| agent \| system | no | — | — | Claimed action source; policy verifies it against the principal. |
| idempotencyKey | string | yes | — | min 1 chars | Unique retry key for this semantic command. |
| correlationId | string | no | — | min 1 chars | Optional caller correlation identifier. |
| source | studio \| webmcp \| mcp \| system \| agent-tool | no | — | — | Surface that submitted the command. |
| sessionId | string | no | — | min 1 chars | Calling session identity. |
| actorId | string | no | — | min 1 chars | Authenticated or local stable actor identity. |

```json
{
  "type": "run_scenario",
  "scenario": {
    "id": "example-id",
    "seed": 1,
    "horizonSeconds": 1,
    "inputs": {
      "population": 1,
      "arrivalRatePerMinute": 1,
      "serviceRatePerMinute": 1,
      "servers": 1
    }
  },
  "idempotencyKey": "example-command-001"
}
```

## Output

A deterministic-seed Simulation Run; it never becomes Constraint Validation.

| Output field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| status | Published result field. |
| runId | Stable identifier. |
| scenarioId | Stable identifier. |
| branchId | Stable identifier. |
| inputFingerprint | Published result field. |
| cacheHit | Published result field. |
| result | Published result field. |
| receipt | Published result field. |

| idempotencyKey | string | yes | — | min 1 chars | Unique retry key for this semantic command. |
| correlationId | string | no | — | min 1 chars | Optional caller correlation identifier. |
| source | studio \| webmcp \| mcp \| system \| agent-tool | no | — | — | Surface that submitted the command. |
| sessionId | string | no | — | min 1 chars | Calling session identity. |
| actorId | string | yes | — | min 1 chars | Authenticated or local stable actor identity. |

```json
{
  "type": "waive_warning",
  "constraintId": "constraint-example",
  "reasonCode": "operational-acceptance",
  "actor": "human",
  "actorId": "actor-example",
  "idempotencyKey": "example-command-001"
}
```

Human-authored warning disposition bound to one Validation input.

| Output field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| status | Published result field. |
| waiverId | Stable identifier. |
| constraintId | Stable identifier. |
| proposalId | Stable identifier. |
| validationInputFingerprint | Published result field. |

- Stable ID: waiverId
- Stable ID: constraintId
- Stable ID: proposalId

## Applicable errors

| Code | Message | Remediation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| COMMAND_INVALID | Venue command requires a type. | Send one published Venue command with its required fields. |
| COMMAND_UNSUPPORTED | Venue command is not supported. | Refresh the command contract and use a published command type. |
| AUTHORIZATION_DENIED | The current principal is not authorized for this VenueMind action. | Use an assigned Organization Membership Role or an active Organization- and Project-scoped Agent Grant containing the required permission. |
| IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED | Idempotency key is required for mutating commands. | Retry with one stable idempotency key for this semantic action. |
| IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT | Idempotency key conflict. | Use the original command input or generate a new idempotency key. |
| WARNING_NOT_WAIVABLE | Constraint does not have a waivable warning. | Validate again and select an open warning Constraint. |
| WAIVER_REASON_INVALID | Warning Waiver requires a supported reason code. | Choose one reason code from the Warning Waiver contract. |

- [Complete error catalog](/docs/reference-errors)
